key_insight: PR3DICTR is an open, modular framework that standardises end-to-end development of 3D medical image classification and outcome prediction models, enabling rapid, reproducible prototyping using community tools (PyTorch, MONAI).
problem_solved: Addresses fragmentation and reproducibility gaps in 3D medical imaging research by providing a unified, configurable pipeline for data handling, modelling, training, evaluation and deployment.
method: Modular pipeline built on PyTorch and MONAI for 3D image input, preprocessing, augmentation, model definition, training and evaluation.
Standardised training recipes and configurable components (data loaders, losses, metrics, schedulers) to simplify reproducible experiments and comparisons.
Support for outcome prediction and classification workflows with hooks for explainability (saliency/heatmaps), logging and export for inference/clinical integration.
impact: Makes 3D medical imaging research more accessible and reproducible, reducing engineering overhead so ML practitioners can iterate faster and compare methods fairly for clinical translation.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: modular components (data → preprocess → model → train → evaluate → deploy) with interchangeability icons
Pipeline flowchart showing one-click configuration / training cycle and standardized outputs (metrics, checkpoints, explainability maps)
Example visuals: side-by-side 3D volume slices with model predictions and saliency overlays
Comparison bar chart: time-to-prototype and reproducibility metrics vs custom/private codebases
paper_title: PR3DICTR: A modular AI framework for medical 3D image-based detection and outcome prediction
paper_authors: Daniel C. MacRae, Luuk van der Hoek, Robert van der Wal, Suzanne P. M. de Vette, Hendrike Neh
